ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Optimality gap of a Transformer tour solver against model width on fixed-size instances
PROPOSAL: Train an encoder-decoder Transformer on uniform random Euclidean instances with 50 cities in the unit square, using supervised imitation of Concorde tours. Vary the embedding width over 64, 128, 256, 512 and 1024 with depth fixed at 6 layers, training each model until validation loss stops improving. Report the mean optimality gap on 2000 fresh instances against parameter count, with three seeds per width. Fit a saturating power law gap = a * P^(-b) + c and read c as the capacity-limited floor.
CONTROLS: Compare against nearest-neighbour, farthest insertion and 2-opt heuristics, and against the width-64 model trained on 10 times more instances to confirm data is not the bottleneck. Check the fit on a held-out width.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The gap should fall close to a power law in width and bend toward a floor around 1 percent; the fit could fail if optimization difficulty, not capacity, dominates at the widest models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Capacity ladder for a Transformer solver of 50-city tours with fine width and depth steps
PROPOSAL: Train an encoder-decoder Transformer on random 50-city Euclidean instances with supervised Concorde targets. Use a ladder of 12 embedding widths from 32 to 2048 in even logarithmic steps, crossed with 4 depths between 2 and 8 layers and 10 seeds in each cell, training each model with a cosine decay schedule fixed in advance. Evaluate on 20000 fresh instances, report the gap versus parameter count with the per-seed spread, and fit a saturating power law to each depth. Keep checkpoints from the end of each stage for diagnosis of failed fits, and log gradient norms at the start of each stage.
CONTROLS: Compare against nearest-neighbour and 2-opt heuristics, and against a width-32 model given a longer schedule. Report spread statistics over the full set of trained models.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Deeper models should shift the curve down by a constant factor; the saturating fit could be unstable at the smallest widths where the schedule is too short.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dependence of achievable tour quality on the number of cities at fixed capacity
PROPOSAL: Fix a Transformer solver at 8 million parameters and train it on Euclidean instances whose city count N takes the values 20, 40, 80, 160, 320 and 640, each trained close to convergence with imitation of Concorde or LKH tours. Record the optimality gap on 1000 held-out instances per N, with 3 seeds. Plot the gap against log N and fit linear, power and logarithmic forms, testing which one describes the growth of the solution space. Training length grows with N until validation loss is flat for 10 consecutive checks.
CONTROLS: Compare with a 2-opt heuristic and with a model of 4 times the parameters at N = 320 to separate capacity limits from optimization limits. Keep training instances at 5 million per N so data does not constrain.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The gap should rise smoothly and sub-linearly with N; the functional form could change past N = 320 where the supervised labels become approximate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gap growth of a mid-sized neural tour solver on instances of 20 to 640 cities with many training variants
PROPOSAL: Take a Transformer solver of 8 million parameters and train it on Euclidean instances with 20, 40, 80, 160, 320 and 640 cities, labelled by Concorde or LKH tours. For each city count, train with 4 learning rates and 3 batch sizes with 5 seeds, each model lasting the same number of steps regardless of city count. Evaluate on 5000 held-out instances per N, and fit linear, power and logarithmic forms to the best model and to the median model. Add a model with training instances drawn from a mixture of all six sizes. Report the spread over seeds per city count in a table.
CONTROLS: Compare with 2-opt and with a 4 times wider model at N = 320. Evaluate the mixture-trained model on each size separately and report its gap beside the single-size models.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The gap should grow sub-linearly with N; best-model and median-model fits could diverge at the largest N where short schedules truncate learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Effect of embedding dimension on a learned solver's tour quality at constant city count
PROPOSAL: Generate Euclidean instances with 40 cities placed uniformly in a d-dimensional unit cube for d equal to 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12, with optimal or near-optimal tours from Concorde on the exact distance matrix. Train a Transformer with 16 million parameters on each d until the gap stops falling, 2 seeds each. Report the optimality gap against d on 2000 fresh instances and fit gap = a + b * d^c. This isolates growth of the representation space while the number of cities stays fixed.
CONTROLS: Compare with a greedy nearest-neighbour baseline and a 2-opt baseline in each dimension, to see whether the heuristics degrade with d as well. Include a model fed only distance matrices with no coordinates.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The gap should rise gently with d as distances concentrate; the trend could flatten if the model learns distance-based shortcuts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Behaviour of a learned solver as coordinates grow from 2 to 12 dimensions with a thorough training protocol
PROPOSAL: Create instances of 40 points uniformly in a d-dimensional unit cube for d from 2 to 12, solved to near-optimality by Concorde. Train a Transformer with 16 million parameters on each d using 6 learning-rate settings and 4 seeds, and score checkpoints saved after every pass through the data on 10000 fresh instances. Report the optimality gap against d from the best checkpoint of each setting and fit gap = a + b * d^c to each setting separately, then compare the exponents c between settings.
CONTROLS: Compare with greedy nearest-neighbour and 2-opt baselines in each dimension. Include models given only distance matrices and models given only coordinates.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The gap should rise gently with d; the fits could disagree on the exponent c, and the largest d may show noisy checkpoints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training-algorithm dependence of the capacity-limited floor on tour optimization
PROPOSAL: Compare how three training methods limit a fixed-capacity solver on 100-city Euclidean instances: supervised imitation of Concorde tours, REINFORCE with a greedy rollout baseline, and a population-based self-improvement loop. Use one architecture with 12 million parameters, give each method training long enough for validation reward to be flat over 20 evaluations, and measure the final optimality gap on 2000 instances with 3 seeds. Repeat the comparison at 25 and 400 cities.
CONTROLS: Control for data volume by matching the number of instances seen. Compare against 2-opt and against a solver whose width is doubled, to ask whether the method gap exceeds the capacity gap.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: Imitation should reach the lowest floor and REINFORCE the highest; the ordering could reverse at 400 cities where labels are costly and rollouts are cheap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Method comparison for training a small solver on tours of 100 cities, with long schedules per variant
PROPOSAL: Evaluate supervised imitation, REINFORCE with a greedy baseline, and a self-improvement loop on 100-city Euclidean instances, using one 12 million parameter architecture. Each method is trained with 5 learning rates, 4 entropy or temperature settings and 3 seeds, always with a long schedule, then scored on 10000 instances. Run the comparison again at 25 and 400 cities, and report the gap with confidence intervals per combination of method and setting. Store checkpoints from the middle of training. Log gradient norms at the start of each epoch for later diagnosis.
CONTROLS: Compare against 2-opt and against a width-doubled model. Report the checkpoints next to the final scores to track drift in the ranking.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: Imitation should reach the lowest gap; the intervals could overlap for REINFORCE and self-improvement, leaving the middle ranking undecided.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does a power law fitted on small solvers predict the gap of a much bigger one
PROPOSAL: Train Transformer solvers with 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 million parameters on 30-city Euclidean instances, 3 seeds each, until the gap stops improving, using supervised Concorde labels. Fit a power law with floor to the gap against parameter count using only these four sizes, then predict the gap of a 64 million parameter model and train that model once to check the prediction. Report the relative prediction error and a bootstrap interval over the fit.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model of 16 million parameters used as an interpolation check, and against a constant-gap prediction. Fit with and without the floor term.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The prediction should land within 15 percent of the observed gap; the prediction could miss badly if the floor is poorly constrained by four small points.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extrapolating solver quality from small models to one of 64 million parameters with a ladder of training runs
PROPOSAL: Train Transformer solvers at 8 scales between 0.25 and 4 million parameters on 30-city Euclidean instances, with 8 seeds per size, using Concorde labels. Fit a power law with floor to the median gap over the scales, plus bootstrap resamples of the seeds, and predict the gap of a 64 million parameter model. Train that model with 5 different seeds to check the prediction, and report the prediction error per seed along with its spread across resamples.
CONTROLS: Compare against 16 and 32 million parameter models as interpolation checks, and against a constant-gap prediction. Refit with the floor fixed to zero. Plot each resampled fit against the observed gaps.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The prediction should fall within 15 percent of observed gaps; the zero-floor refit could underpredict the largest model by a visible amount.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Which functional form describes gap growth with city count: model selection among five candidates
PROPOSAL: Collect optimality gaps of a fixed 8 million parameter Transformer solver on instances with 20 to 500 cities at 9 sizes, trained to convergence on Concorde labels with 3 seeds. Fit power, logarithmic, saturating exponential, stretched exponential and linear forms by least squares in log space. Compare forms with leave-one-size-out cross-validation and report which generalizes to the two largest sizes, and which parameters stay stable under resampling of seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare against a null form with a constant gap, and check whether the ranking of forms holds with a 16 million parameter model trained on 5 of the 9 sizes.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Two forms should be hard to separate on the training range but diverge on the largest sizes; the cross-validation could favour a flexible form that overfits nine points.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Functional form of gap growth with city count, fitted to a library of 450 trained solver runs
PROPOSAL: Train an 8 million parameter Transformer solver on instances with 20 to 500 cities at 15 values of N, using Concorde labels, 6 learning rates and 5 seeds, each model lasting a fixed number of steps. Fit power, logarithmic, saturating exponential, stretched exponential and linear forms to the best model, the median model and the mean over seeds. Compare each form on each aggregate with leave-one-size-out cross-validation, and tabulate every parameter estimate with its resampling interval.
CONTROLS: Compare against a constant-gap null, and repeat the fitting procedure on a 16 million parameter model for all the settings.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Forms should rank alike in the best and median aggregates; rankings could split in the mean, which is sensitive to failed models at the largest city counts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Coordinate rotation test separating representation growth from solution-space growth
PROPOSAL: Take 2-dimensional Euclidean instances with 30 cities and embed them into 4, 8 and 16 dimensions by a random orthogonal map, so the optimal tour and the distance matrix are unchanged while the input representation grows. Train a Transformer with 4 million parameters on each embedding, 3 seeds, and measure the optimality gap on 1000 fresh instances. A gap rising with embedding dimension would show a cost of representation alone.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model that receives the distance matrix directly, and against the plain 2-dimensional model. Add a fresh random rotation per instance to check whether the model relies on a fixed axis alignment.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: The gap should stay close to the 2-dimensional value when rotations are fixed; the gap could rise with dimension if the model must learn to discard unused axes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Orthogonal embedding of planar tours into higher dimensions, studied with a wide training protocol
PROPOSAL: Create planar instances of 30 cities and map them into 4, 8 and 16 dimensions by random orthogonal matrices, keeping optimal tours fixed. Train a Transformer with 4 million parameters on each embedding using 5 learning rates, 6 seeds and 3 initial scales, and measure the optimality gap on 10000 fresh instances per setting. Fit the gap against embedding dimension separately per learning rate, and record the training-loss curve of each model. Report how many models diverged.
CONTROLS: Compare against the distance-matrix model and the plain planar model. Use a fresh rotation per instance in half of the runs.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: The gap should be flat in dimension for fixed rotations; learning-rate dependence could obscure a small trend among the many noisy runs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training-length dependence of the gap at fixed capacity until training saturates
PROPOSAL: Train a Transformer solver with 8 million parameters on 100-city Euclidean instances for training lengths of 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 million sampled instances, with Concorde labels and a constant learning rate followed by a final decay. Measure the optimality gap on 2000 fresh instances at each length, 3 seeds. Fit gap = c + a * D^(-b) and report the point at which additional data stops helping, which identifies the capacity limit at this size.
CONTROLS: Compare against 2-opt, and against a 32 million parameter model trained on 8 million instances, to show the floor moves with capacity. Check for overfitting by drawing instances without repetition.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The gap should flatten after about 16 million instances at this size; the floor could still be falling slowly if optimization has not converged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training-length study of a solver of 8 million parameters on 100-city tours, up to well beyond saturation
PROPOSAL: Train an 8 million parameter Transformer on 100-city Euclidean instances for 12 training lengths between 2 and 128 million sampled instances, with Concorde labels, 4 learning-rate schedules and 5 seeds. Measure the optimality gap on 10000 fresh instances after each model and fit gap = c + a * D^(-b) to each schedule. Report where each curve flattens, and give the final gap of each model in a table with its seed band.
CONTROLS: Compare against 2-opt, and against a 32 million parameter model trained at those lengths. Draw instances without repetition.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Curves should flatten by about 16 million instances with all schedules; lengths beyond 64 million may reveal only noise around the floor.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distance concentration in high dimension and its link to learned-solver gaps
PROPOSAL: Measure, for uniform random points in d dimensions with d equal to 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32, the ratio between the largest and smallest pairwise distance among 50 points, and relate it to the optimality gap of a 6 million parameter Transformer trained at each d on Concorde labels, 3 seeds. Report the correlation between concentration and gap, and fit the gap as a function of the ratio. This tests the explanation that curse of dimensionality drives degradation.
CONTROLS: Compare against 2-opt, whose gap does not depend on learning, and against a model trained on clustered points where the concentration ratio is held at its 2-dimensional value.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The gap should correlate strongly with concentration; the link could vanish for clustered data, pointing to a different mechanism.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pairwise-distance statistics for dimensions 2 to 32 alongside a thorough set of trained solver models
PROPOSAL: For uniform points in d dimensions with 9 values of d between 2 and 32, measure the ratio of largest to smallest pairwise distance among 50 points, then train a 6 million parameter Transformer on Concorde labels at each d, with 6 learning rates and 5 seeds. Evaluate 10000 instances per model and fit the gap to the ratio, to dimension, and to log dimension per learning rate. Add 4 normalisation variants of the input in the first three dimensions.
CONTROLS: Compare against 2-opt, and against a model trained on clustered points, where the concentration ratio stays near its planar value.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The gap should correlate with the ratio with all learning rates; correlations could fade among the runs when training has not converged at high dimension.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned solver gap relative to classical heuristics as problem size grows
PROPOSAL: Compare a trained Transformer solver of 10 million parameters with farthest insertion, Christofides and 2-opt with neighbour lists on Euclidean instances of 50, 100, 200, 400 and 800 cities, 1000 instances per size. The solver is trained per size on Concorde labels to convergence, 2 seeds. Report optimality gap and its ratio to the best heuristic against city count, and find the size where the learned solver loses its edge.
CONTROLS: Compare solver variants of 5 and 20 million parameters at 400 cities to see if the crossover moves with capacity. Test heuristics with identical random starts.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The solver should beat insertion at small sizes and lose to 2-opt at 800 cities; the crossover could be capacity-dependent and move upward with more parameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Head-to-head comparison of a neural tour solver with four heuristic families at five city counts, with extended tuning
PROPOSAL: Compare a trained 10 million parameter Transformer with farthest insertion, Christofides, 2-opt and Or-opt on Euclidean instances of 50, 100, 200, 400 and 800 cities, 10000 instances per size. Train the solver per size with 5 learning rates and 4 seeds on one long schedule, and tune each heuristic over 8 restart and neighbour-list settings. Report the gap and the ratio to the best tuned heuristic against city count.
CONTROLS: Compare solver variants of 5 and 20 million parameters at 400 cities. Test heuristics with random restarts each.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The solver should beat insertion at small sizes only; tuning grids could shift each crossover by one step in city count, blurring where the edge ends.
